prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1213; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received from the policyholder's driver reporting a low-speed head-on collision in a parking area, with a back strain as the reported injury. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been asked to confirm the policy details, which match our records.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photos submitted by the claimant. They confirm some details of the impact, and the damage shown on the vehicle is consistent with the described collision. No independent witnesses have come forward, but the police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant again today. The account of how the collision happened matched what was given at first report, with the same sequence of events and the same details. No prior damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 4: Checked medical records provided by the claimant. The back strain fits the kind and force of a low-speed impact, and no earlier injury to the same area appears in the history. Treatment followed a usual course and eased off as the claimant improved.

Entry 5: Compared the repair estimate with the damage visible in the photos and the described impact. The scope of repairs lines up well with what the collision would be expected to cause. No concerns raised about the vehicle's condition before the loss.

Entry 6: File reviewed and all items on hand. The claimant's account stayed consistent throughout, the injury, vehicle damage, and coverage timing all fit the facts reported, and the claim is ready for the next settlement step.
